summary: This Wikipedia-derived note profiles Al Holland, a relief pitcher whose best season was with the Philadelphia Phillies, when he won the Rolaids Relief Man of the Year and TSN Fireman of the Year awards. It then covers his key 1983 postseason appearances, including saves in Game 1 of the NL Championship Series and Game 1 of the World Series, and the Phillies' loss to the Baltimore Orioles in the World Series. The year of his best season is missing from the note.
one_line: Al Holland was a relief pitcher whose top season with the Philadelphia Phillies and 1983 postseason performances, including the World Series loss to the Baltimore Orioles, are recounted.
key_facts: Al Holland finished seventh in the National League Rookie of the Year voting for 1980.
Al Holland won the Rolaids Relief Man of the Year Award and the TSN Fireman of the Year Award during his best season with the Philadelphia Phillies.
In his best season with the Philadelphia Phillies, Al Holland finished in the top ten in voting for both the Cy Young Award and National League MVP.
Al Holland saved Game 1 of the 1983 National League Championship Series.
Al Holland struck out three batters in two innings to finish Game 4 of the 1983 National League Championship Series, clinching the pennant for the Philadelphia Phillies.
Al Holland saved Game 1 of the 1983 World Series.
In Game 3 of the 1983 World Series, Al Holland was pitching in the seventh inning when an error allowed the go-ahead run to score.
Al Holland struck out four batters in the eighth and ninth innings of Game 3 of the 1983 World Series, but the Philadelphia Phillies lost.
Game 3 of the 1983 World Series was the last postseason game of Al Holland's career.
The Philadelphia Phillies then lost Games 4 and 5 of the 1983 World Series, giving the Baltimore Orioles the championship.
